name: PREM
description: The Preliminary Reference Earth Model as published, evaluated on the nodes of PREM-stable. GIAMIP uses PREM-stable in its place (protocol v4.0 Section 3.1). This file is kept to compare the two and to identify runs made with the published PREM.

source.citation: Dziewonski, A. M. and Anderson, D. L. (1981). Preliminary reference Earth model. Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 25(4), 297-356.
source.evaluated_by: Ghelichkhan, S., Hoggard, M. and Scott, W. (2026). PREM-stable: a gravitationally stable PREM for GIA models (Version v1.0.0) [Dataset]. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.23178246

profile.order: Rows go from the centre of the Earth (radius 0) to the surface (radius 6371 km).
profile.discontinuities: A boundary between two PREM regions has two rows at the same radius. The first row holds the value below the boundary and the second the value above.
profile.interpolation: Linear in radius between two neighbouring rows. Between the surface and the core-mantle boundary the gravity column is computed for density that varies linearly between nodes. In the core, mass and gravity come from the PREM polynomials, and linear interpolation of gravity there differs from them by up to about 1.2e-4 of the value.
profile.spacing: At most 10 km between the surface and the core-mantle boundary, and at most 100 km in the core.

columns.name: depth_km
columns.quantity: depth below the surface, 6371 km minus the radius

columns.name: region
columns.quantity: index of the PREM region of Dziewonski and Anderson (1981), Table I, counted from the centre

notes: Evaluated from the polynomial coefficients of Table I of Dziewonski and Anderson (1981), at a reference period of 1 s, with no attenuation.

Between 24.4 and 220 km depth PREM is transversely isotropic. This file uses the isotropic wave speeds of the footnote of Table I, V_P = 4.1875 + 3.9382x and V_S = 2.1519 + 2.3481x km/s, with x the radius divided by 6371 km.

The 3 km ocean layer of PREM is replaced by upper crust (2600 kg/m3, V_P 5.8 km/s, V_S 3.2 km/s) up to the surface. A GIA model applies the ocean as a surface load, so the Earth model has no fluid layer at the top.
PREM is gravitationally unstable where the mantle flows, most strongly between 24.4 and 220 km depth. See prem-stable.
